metadata.status: DRAFT: answers must be reviewed by a person (ideally a mortgage expert) before use
metadata.about: 72 questions derived from 9 use cases (ids UC1-01 ... UC9-08, 8 per use case). Many describe a client's application and ask whether it is acceptable; the use cases are explained in docs/USE_CASES.md.
metadata.unanswerable: Category 'unanswerable': the policy does not contain the answer, or the question lacks facts needed to decide. A correct answer says so (and names what is missing) instead of guessing.
metadata.page_numbering: page = physical PDF page (1-95), not the printed page label
metadata.quote_normalization: Quotes are copied from the PDF text. Line-break hyphenation and whitespace were joined.

questions.question: A client buys a houseboat with a fixed mooring rented from the municipality. The boat is valued at €300,000 and the mooring at €50,000; the valuation report gives an expected lifetime of 25 years. The client asks for €320,000, of which €80,000 interest-only, over 30 years. Is this acceptable? Name every rule that is broken.
questions.answer: No. Four rules are broken: (1) the maximum loan is 90% of the boat (€270,000) plus 90% of the mooring (€45,000) = €315,000, so €320,000 is too high; (2) interest-only is not allowed for a houseboat; (3) the boat loan must be repaid within the expected lifetime of 25 years, so 30 years is too long; (4) the loan on the mooring must be repaid in 20 years. Not given in the case: whether the boat is in the ship register and has a shore connection.

evidence.quote: De maximale verstrekkingsnorm is 90% van de marktwaarde van de woonboot en 90% van de marktwaarde van de ligplaats (de ligplaats hoeft hiervoor niet in eigendom te zijn).
Aflossingsvrij lenen is niet toegestaan.
De lening op de woonboot wordt binnen de verwachte levensduur van de woonboot volledig afgelost, met een maximum van 30 jaar. De verwachte levensduur blijkt uit het taxatierapport.
De lening op de ligplaats wordt in 20 jaar volledig afgelost.

questions.hop_reasoning: All four limits are in 5.5.12, but the question does not name them: each case fact has to be checked against a different sentence of the section.

questions.question: Can part of a houseboat mortgage be interest-only?
questions.answer: No. Interest-only borrowing is not allowed for a houseboat with a fixed mooring.

questions.question: A houseboat is valued at €300,000 and its mooring at €50,000. What is the maximum loan?
questions.answer: €315,000: 90% of the boat (€270,000) plus 90% of the mooring (€45,000). The mooring does not have to be owned for this.

evidence.quote: De maximale verstrekkingsnorm is 90% van de marktwaarde van de woonboot en 90% van de marktwaarde van de ligplaats (de ligplaats hoeft hiervoor niet in eigendom te zijn).

questions.question: Same houseboat (boat €300,000, mooring €50,000, expected lifetime 25 years, E.M.C.I. valuation, in the ship register, shore connection, municipal mooring). The client now asks €315,000, fully annuity, over 25 years. Is it acceptable now?
questions.answer: Not yet. Amount (€315,000 = the maximum), repayment type and the 25-year boat term are now fine, but the loan on the mooring must be repaid in 20 years. With one term of 25 years for the whole loan, the mooring part breaks that rule; the mooring part needs a term of at most 20 years.

questions.question: Same houseboat (boat €300,000, mooring €50,000, expected lifetime 25 years, E.M.C.I. valuation, in the ship register, shore connection, municipal mooring). Loan €315,000, fully annuity, term 20 years. Does it meet the houseboat rules?
questions.answer: Yes. €315,000 is exactly the maximum (90% of €300,000 + 90% of €50,000), there is no interest-only part, 20 years is within the 25-year lifetime and meets the 20-year mooring rule, and the boat conditions (ship register, shore connection, government mooring, E.M.C.I. valuation) are met.

questions.answer: An E.M.C.I.-certified houseboat appraiser, with separate values for the boat and the mooring. NWWI validation is not required.

questions.question: Regular house, €600,000 from a validated valuation report. The loan of €450,000 has three parts: €100,000 interest-only, €200,000 savings mortgage whose savings product is NOT pledged, and €150,000 annuity. Does this stay within the interest-only limit?
questions.answer: No. Because the savings product is not pledged, the whole €200,000 part counts as interest-only. Total interest-only is €300,000, above the cap of €150,000 (the lower of 30% of €600,000 = €180,000 and €150,000).

evidence.quote: Aflossingsvrij lenen is toegestaan tot maximaal 30% van de marktwaarde van de woning en niet meer dan € 150.000.

Een aflossingsvrij gedeelte als onderdeel van de hypotheek met opbouwproduct (verkapt aflossingsvrij lenen) wordt ook gezien als aflossingsvrij en telt daardoor mee voor het maximale percentage en bedrag.
Als het opbouwproduct niet is verpand, dan wordt de gehele lening gezien als aflossingsvrij.

questions.hop_reasoning: The cap and the 'hidden interest-only' rule are both in 1.1.3, but in different paragraphs; reading only the cap gives the wrong answer.

questions.question: A savings mortgage part has a savings product that is not pledged. How much of that loan part counts as interest-only?
questions.answer: All of it: if the build-up product is not pledged, the whole loan part is treated as interest-only.

questions.answer: Yes. With a pledged product the interest-only share follows from the target capital; if that covers the €200,000, none of it is interest-only. Total interest-only is then €100,000, within the €150,000 cap.

questions.answer: That cannot be decided with these facts. The answer depends on (1) the market value of the home (the cap is 30% of it, at most €150,000) and (2) whether the savings product is pledged (if not, the full €100,000 also counts as interest-only, giving €220,000, which is above €150,000 in any case).

questions.question: Detached house with a market value of €400,000 from a Rabobank Desktop Taxatie of Calcasa. The client needs a €380,000 mortgage. Is that within the maximum loan-to-value, and if not, what can the advisor do?
questions.answer: No. With a desktop valuation the maximum is 90% = €360,000, and a desktop valuation is not even possible for a loan above 90% of the value. The advisor can order an NWWI-validated valuation report: then the maximum is 100% = €400,000 and €380,000 fits.

questions.question: List all situations in which a Rabobank Desktop Taxatie (Plus) of Calcasa cannot be used.
questions.answer: (1) The collateral is a farmhouse, home with shop or practice, business dwelling, mobile home, water home, houseboat, recreation home or let home. (2) It was delivered in the current or previous calendar year. (3) There is a ground lease (erfpacht) or right of superficies (opstal), unless the opstal is for a utility. (4) There is a purchase scheme (koopoplossing), except the SVn Starterslening. (5) The reliability level of the desktop valuation is below 5. (6) The market value is above €1 million. (7) The loan is more than 90% of the market value. In addition, the standard (non-Plus) desktop valuation is not allowed when the client has or wants interest-only borrowing.

Er is sprake van een koopoplossing. Met uitzondering van de SVn Starterslening, dan is een Rabobank Desktop Taxatie (Plus) van Calcasa wel toegestaan.
Het betrouwbaarheidsniveau van de Rabobank Desktop Taxatie (Plus) van Calcasa is lager dan 5.
De marktwaarde van de woning is hoger dan € 1 miljoen.
De benodigde of totale lening is meer dan 90% van de marktwaarde van het onderpand.
